title: Parallel Resonance Circuit (Tank Circuit)
short_intro: A parallel resonance circuit consists of an inductor with internal resistance in parallel with a capacitor across an alternating voltage source. At resonance, the circuit impedance is maximum and the reactive currents cancel out, resulting in a minimum supply current.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Definition of parallel resonance, condition for resonance (frequency formula), phase relationship between voltage and total current, and maximum impedance condition for an ideal LC parallel circuit.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Exact resonant frequency for a real inductor with resistance r, dynamic impedance expression, sharpness of resonance, bandwidth, and quality factor (Q-factor) derivations.

prerequisites: Alternating current fundamentals and phasor algebra
Complex impedance and admittance of series LCR circuits
Condition of electrical resonance in series AC circuits

concept_notes.heading: Basic Structure of Parallel Resonance
bullets: Comprises a capacitor of capacitance C connected in parallel with an inductive coil having inductance L and resistance r.
The alternating source supplies a total current which splits into the inductive branch current and capacitive branch current.
Serves as a rejector circuit because it offers maximum impedance and minimum current at the resonant frequency.

concept_notes.heading: Condition for Resonance in a Parallel Circuit
bullets: Resonance occurs when the reactive component of the total admittance of the circuit becomes zero.
Alternatively, it is defined as the frequency at which the total current is in phase with the applied alternating voltage, making the power factor unity.
The resonant frequency depends on whether the inductive coil resistance r is negligible or substantial.

concept_notes.heading: Dynamic Impedance at Resonance
bullets: At resonance, the parallel combination exhibits a very high pure resistive impedance known as dynamic impedance.
For a coil with negligible resistance (r approx 0), the dynamic impedance approaches infinity, reducing the supply current to zero.
For a practical coil with resistance r, the dynamic impedance is given by L / (C r).

concept_notes.heading: Bandwidth and Quality Factor (Q-factor)
bullets: The quality factor Q of a parallel resonant circuit is the ratio of circulating reactive current through the LC tank to the external supply current.
Q-factor determines the sharpness of the resonance curve and is expressed as (omega<sub>0</sub> L) / r.
Bandwidth (Delta omega) is inversely proportional to the Q-factor, given by Delta omega = omega<sub>0</sub> / Q.

derivations.title: Resonant Frequency and Dynamic Impedance for a Practical Parallel Circuit
derivations.conditions: Inductive branch contains inductor L and series resistance r in parallel with ideal capacitor C.
steps: Write the complex impedance of the inductive branch as Z_L = r + j\omega L and the capacitive branch as Z_C = -j / (\omega C).
Express the total admittance Y as the sum of admittances: Y = Y_L + Y_C = \frac{1}{r + j\omega L} + j\omega C.
Rationalize the inductive admittance: Y_L = \frac{r - j\omega L}{r^2 + \omega^2 L^2}.
Equate the imaginary part of the total admittance to zero for resonance: \frac{\omega L}{r^2 + \omega^2 L^2} = \omega C.
Solve for resonant frequency: \omega_0^2 = \frac{1}{LC} - \frac{r^2}{L^2}, giving f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\frac{1}{LC} - \frac{r^2}{L^2}}.
derivations.result: Resonant frequency omega_0 = \sqrt{\frac{1}{LC} - \frac{r^2}{L^2}} and dynamic impedance Z_d = \frac{L}{Cr}.

derivations.title: Quality Factor of Parallel Resonance Circuit
derivations.conditions: Parallel L-C-r circuit driven by a constant voltage source V.
steps: Define Q-factor as the ratio of peak reactive power to average power dissipated per radian, or the magnification of current.
Circulating current in the LC loop at resonance is I_c = \frac{V}{\omega_0 L}, and supply current is I = \frac{V}{Z_d} = \frac{Vr}{L}.
Substitute Z_d = L / (Cr) and inductive reactance X_L = \omega_0 L.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Frequency vs Impedance Curve (Rejector Circuit)
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A bell-shaped curve plotting Impedance (Z) on the y-axis against Frequency (f) on the x-axis, peaking sharply at f_0.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Impedance is minimum at very low and very high frequencies, reaching a sharp maximum value Z_d at the resonant frequency f_0.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Tested conceptually in TGT/PGT to identify parallel resonance as a rejector circuit.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Frequency vs Supply Current Curve
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A trough-shaped curve plotting Total Current (I) on the y-axis against Frequency (f) on the x-axis, showing a sharp minimum at f_0.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: The total supply current drops to its lowest value at resonance because the parallel LC branches draw equal and opposite reactive currents.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Used to differentiate acceptor (series) and rejector (parallel) resonance behavior.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Phase Angle vs Frequency
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: S-shaped curve showing phase angle phi transitioning from positive (inductive at low frequencies) through zero at f_0 to negative (capacitive at high frequencies).
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: At resonance, the phase angle between voltage and current is zero, making the circuit purely resistive (unity power factor).
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Questions on power factor and phase conditions at resonance.

solved_numericals.question: A parallel resonant circuit has an inductor of 2 H and a capacitor of 2 micro-Farad with negligible resistance. Calculate the resonant frequency.
solution_steps: Identify given values: L = 2 H, C = 2 \times 10^{-6} F.
Use the ideal parallel resonance formula: f_0 = \frac{1}{2 \pi \sqrt{LC}}.
Square root of LC is 2 \times 10^{-3} s.

solved_numericals.question: An inductive coil of inductance 0.5 H and resistance 20 ohm is connected in parallel with a variable capacitor across a 230 V, 50 Hz supply. Find the capacitance required for resonance and the dynamic impedance.
solution_steps: Given L = 0.5 H, r = 20 \Omega, f = 50 Hz, so \omega = 2 \pi f = 100 \pi \approx 314.16 rad/s.
Use exact resonance condition for practical parallel circuit: \omega^2 = \frac{1}{LC} - \frac{r^2}{L^2}.
Solve for C: C = \frac{1}{100296 \times 0.5} = \frac{1}{50148} \approx 1.994 \times 10^{-5} F = 19.94 \mu F.

solved_numericals.question: A parallel L-C-r circuit has L = 0.2 H, C = 50 micro-Farad, and r = 10 ohm. Determine the Q-factor of the circuit at resonance.
solution_steps: Calculate resonant angular frequency using \omega_0 \approx \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} since r is relatively small: \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{0.2 \times 50 \times 10^{-6}}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{10^{-5}}} = \frac{1}{3.162 \times 10^{-3}} \approx 316.22 rad/s.
Use the Q-factor formula for parallel circuits: Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{r}.

assumptions_and_limitations: Assumes sinusoidal AC source operating at steady state conditions.
Stray capacitances between inductor turns are neglected in basic derivations.
The formula omega_0 = 1/sqrt(LC) is an approximation valid only when the coil resistance r is much smaller than sqrt(L/C).

common_misconceptions.wrong: Parallel resonance occurs when inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance (omega L = 1 / omega C).
common_misconceptions.correct: This condition applies to series resonance; parallel resonance requires zero imaginary admittance, leading to a modified frequency formula.
common_misconceptions.why: The presence of resistance in the inductive branch alters the phase of the branch current, shifting the true resonance frequency from the ideal LC value.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Parallel resonance circuits have minimum impedance at resonance.
common_misconceptions.correct: Parallel resonance circuits have maximum impedance (dynamic impedance) at resonance.
common_misconceptions.why: Because it acts as a rejector circuit, it impedes line current flow at resonance, opposite to series circuits.

quick_revision: Parallel resonance is a rejector circuit offering maximum impedance and minimum supply current at resonance.
Exact resonant frequency for a real parallel circuit is f_0 = (1 / 2 pi) sqrt(1/LC - r^2/L^2).
Dynamic impedance at resonance is given by Z_d = L / (C r).
Quality factor Q = omega_0 L / r measures both sharpness of resonance and current magnification in the tank loop.
